prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Database column specification for orders table (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Column" · longest unbreakable word 137px · one-line width 137px
  col 2: header "Type" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 210px
  col 3: header "Nullable" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 161px · one-line width 161px
  col 5: header "Comment" · longest unbreakable word 93px · one-line width 577px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A reference spec of the orders table's columns — an engineering artifact read to answer 'what columns exist, what type, can it be null, what's the default, what does it mean'. It is consulted, not compared numerically; the reader jumps to a column name and then reads across that row.","reading":"Top-to-bottom scan of the Column column (identifiers are the index), then a rightward read of that row's Type / Nullable / Default, with Comment read only when needed. Cross-row comparison of Type values is secondary but real (repeated BIGINT UNSIGNED, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE).","groups":["Column + Type form the identity pair — always read together and must never be broken mid-token","Nullable + Default form the constraint pair — both are short flag-like values, low information density, safe to keep narrow","Comment is prose, a separate register, and can absorb wrapping at line breaks"],"keep_intact":["column identifiers (order_reference, total_amount_cents, cancelled_at) — snake_case split across lines is misread as two columns","type tokens (BIGINT UNSIGNED, VARCHAR(32), TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE) — breaking at spaces is tolerable, breaking inside a word is not","default literals (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) — a single token, must not split","Nullable YES/NO — 3 characters, never wrap"],"may_wrap":["Comment — free prose, wraps at word boundaries with no loss","Type — may wrap between its words (TIMESTAMP / WITH TIME ZONE) if words stay whole","Default — may wrap to two lines if the token itself stays intact"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [140, 80, 44, 46, 49] · table 360×4466px · row heights [83, 525, 455, 618, 618, 571, 478, 571, 548] · column headers wrapped 3/5 · tallest cell 26 lines · mid-word splits 120
Design r0B: widths [158, 231, 80, 182, 200] · table 852×839px · row heights [36, 106, 83, 106, 106, 106, 83, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 492px
Design r0C: widths [158, 231, 80, 182, 598] · table 1250×327px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 890px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
